residencyRequirements.description: Either party must be domiciled in Nigeria at the time of filing (MCA s.2). A wife who has been ordinarily resident in Nigeria for at least 3 years immediately preceding the petition is deemed domiciled in Nigeria (MCA s.7(b)). Any person domiciled in Nigeria may file in the High Court of any state (MCA s.2(3)); the Cross River State High Court is the usual venue when either party resides within the state.

waitingPeriod.description: Decree Nisi becomes Decree Absolute automatically after 3 months (MCA s.58); where there are children under 16, subject to the court's s.57 declaration on arrangements for them. Cannot petition within 2 years of marriage without leave (MCA s.30); the bar does not apply to petitions based on wilful refusal to consummate, adultery, or s.16(1)(a) (s.30(2)).

twoYearBar.description: MCA s.30 — 2-year bar from date of marriage unless exceptional hardship or depravity. Does not apply to petitions based on wilful refusal to consummate (s.15(2)(a)), adultery (s.15(2)(b)) or s.16(1)(a), or to cross-proceedings (s.30(2)).

noFault.name: 2-Year Separation with Consent
noFault.description: Lived apart 2+ continuous years immediately before the petition; respondent does not object to a decree.

noFault.name: 3-Year Separation without Consent
noFault.description: Lived apart 3+ continuous years immediately before the petition.

fault.name: Wilful Refusal to Consummate
fault.description: Respondent wilfully and persistently refused to consummate.

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: Respondent committed adultery and the petitioner finds it intolerable to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Intolerable Behaviour
fault.description: Respondent behaved such that the petitioner cannot reasonably be expected to live with the respondent.

fault.name: Desertion for One Year
fault.description: Respondent deserted for a continuous period of 1+ year immediately before the petition.

fault.name: Failure to Comply with Restitution Order
fault.description: Respondent failed to comply with conjugal rights order for 1+ year.

fault.name: Presumption of Death (Absent 7 Years)
fault.description: Reasonable grounds to presume the other party dead (s.15(2)(h)); absence of 7+ years with no reason to believe them alive suffices (s.16(2)(a)).

legalCitations.code: Matrimonial Causes Act 1970, Cap M7 LFN 2004

legalCitations.description: Welfare of the child — adopted by Cross River State

filingFees.notes: Filing fees vary by court registry.

decreeProcess.decreeNisi: Court grants Decree Nisi after hearing.
decreeProcess.decreeAbsolute: Decree Nisi becomes Decree Absolute automatically by force of law 3 months after it is made (MCA s.58); no application is needed. Where there are children under 16, the decree does not become absolute until the court has declared it is satisfied with the arrangements for their welfare (MCA s.57).
